summary: On 9 October 2025 PepsiCo announced the largest redesign in Lay's nearly 100-year history: a warmer sun logo with "Lay's Rays", matte bags with a wood-grain, potato-crate look, a "Made with real potatoes" claim and recipes without artificial flavors or colors in the U.S. The trigger was research that roughly 42% of consumers didn't know the chips are made from potatoes. In Turkey the new pack launched with a local ad film by TBWA\Istanbul (March 2026). Reactions are mixed: the design itself is mostly accepted, but the potato claim, a pack that resembles Lay's Baked and a perceived taste change dominate the conversation.
claim: "Every chip is rooted in real potatoes, real people and real joy" — the redesign should make sure people know Lay's are made with real, farm-grown potatoes, with "the same unbeatable taste."
comparison_targets: Lay's Baked (matte pack, 50% less fat) — the brand's own better-for-you line
Earlier Lay's identities (2007 slices-to-chip, 1965 logo, 2019 refresh)
Lay's Super Bowl LX ad "Last Harvest" (Feb 2026) and the Turkish ad film (Mar 2026)

key_questions: The brand found it was not associated with natural ingredients. Did this rebrand fix that?
